items.anchor: denotes the classical Fr\'echet derivative of $\nabla F$
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M41): the convention names its scope, Theorem art:local-failure-lower and Table art:regularity-map (before: "Here a classical Hessian is ..."). Convention: F has a classical Hessian at x (x is a twice-differentiable point) when F is differentiable on a neighborhood of x and its derivative map is differentiable at x, (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 x, DifferentiableAt ℝ F z) ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x — the form of 'at every twice-differentiable point' in NegativeLower.local_failure_lower. classical_hessian: under the neighborhood condition, the gradient map near x is coordinateGradient F (F has that gradient at every nearby point); differentiability of the derivative map at x is equivalent to differentiability of the gradient map at x; and then RadialHessian.matrix F x, with entries fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x eᵢ eⱼ, is symmetric and is the derivative of the gradient map at x. The neighborhood condition cannot be dropped: fderiv is 0 wherever F is not differentiable, so for instance F(t) = t²·1_ℚ(t) has fderiv ≡ 0, which is differentiable at 0, although F is differentiable at no other point; 'a pointwise second-order expansion alone is not the convention'. resolved_discrepancies.description: Lemma art:seed_cycle states 'With p_j=-M_jg_j, the entire line-search query list is Table art:trial_table' (failure.tex:107-108) without fixing the line-search constants (c₁,c₂), and the query list depends on them. The rejected rows fail Armijo for every c₁ > 0 and the accepted rows pass weak Wolfe for every c₂ > 0, but the accepted row of phase j passes Armijo only for c₁ ≤ r_j = (G(z_j)-G(z_{j+1}))/(-g_jᵀs_j) (Lean: accepted_armijo_iff), and the exact ratios are r₀ ≈ 0.76658, r₁ ≈ 0.39319, r₂ ≈ 0.37521 (Lean: accepted_armijo_ratios, 0.37520 < r₂ < 0.37521). So the claim is false for every c₁ > r₂: the phase-2 trial 1/16 fails Armijo. For example, for c₁ = 0.38, c₂ = 1/2 (0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1) the specified search from (z₂,M₂) does not return (1/16,[1,1/2,1/4,1/8,1/16]) for any trial budget (Lean: seed_cycle_range_counterexample). The range appears only after Table art:trial_table (lines 154-161), as a consequence of the margins ('Hence Armijo holds for c₁ ≤ 1/3 and weak Wolfe holds for every c₂ > 0'), not as a hypothesis of the lemma. With 'for every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0' the claim holds (Lean: seed_cycle, seed_search); this range contains the range 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3, c₁ < c₂ < 1 of Theorems art:local-failure and art:local-failure-lower, so no later result is affected. The rest of the lemma (positive definiteness, the closures, the unique active gradients, the value increase at every rejection, art:seed_margins and art:seed_query_bounds) holds as printed, for all parameters.
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: With $p_j=-M_jg_j$, for every $0<c_1\le1/3$ and $c_2>0$ the entire line-search query list is Table~\ref{art:trial_table}.

The Decision column and the caption's 'deterministic trial tree' (failure.tex:128-143) are decisions of the specified search, which depend on (c₁,c₂), and neither the table nor its caption fixes them. For 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3 and c₂ > 0 every decision is correct (Lean: trial_table, table_decision, seed_search), but for c₁ = 0.38, c₂ = 1/2 the 'accept' of the row (phase 2, α = 1/16) is false: its Armijo ratio lies in (0.37520, 0.37521) (Lean: accepted_armijo_ratios, seed_cycle_range_counterexample). The other cells (phases, trial lengths, value enclosures, active branches) and the other caption claims hold as printed.
